allocation.comparative_reasoning: LEGACY: NO_MATCH for site-native discovery channels and hop-cost scaling. Targeted index screening ('sitemap', 'hop') returned zero hits across the 1,401 artifacts (blob 9bb76113aeaf46d9aecdd8a38349a3a7741e57c3) - an explicit search limitation, not proof of absence; the legacy frontier thread (frontier-collection-calibration holdout kits, artifacts 764-775) concerns collection calibration and holdout construction, not discovery reachability. The nearest guards are P2-WP002B (no website holdout; do not claim cross-site transfer of prediction) and P2-REPLAY-COST (pre2 artifact 4.114, sha 9687ff787f2d74460bb7006826008852f5b4416b: matched tasks and correct denominators). Not a pointless rerun: v1 and v2 never produced a measurement of this question (blocked design and design-contract violation, respectively), and the reframe makes the previously assumed prerequisite the measured object, so the architectural question is finally asked on a pool that actually exists instead of one attested to exist. A third attempt at the identical conditional-reachability design would be duplicative; this is materially distinct.
allocation.question: On the credential-free GET-only stdlib-HTTP substrate, over a broadened frozen multi-host pool enumerated by DESIGN WITHOUT a required engine-count precondition, treat attainability itself as the measured object: (Q1) for each host/engine, how many state-carrying items sit at shortest-path hop >= 3 under the frozen same-host static-<a> BFS (depth <= 6, budget 250), reported per engine with an explicit count of engines that yield ZERO DEEP items; (Q2) conditional on the attained pool, what fraction of those DEEP items is reachable in <= K = 3 fresh-agent GETs (one discovery GET + item-page GET + one spare) via ANY of the five frozen site-native discovery channels (ROBOTS_SITEMAP, SITEMAP_XML, ON_SITE_SEARCH, RSS_ATOM, JSON_LD), with per-channel coverage disclosed and any channel yielding zero admitted DEEP items reported as such rather than counted as a null; and (Q3) is that O(1)-reachable fraction >= 0.50 on at least two distinct hosts/engines? Preregistered decision rule, satisfiable in BOTH directions and never blocked by an unattainable prerequisite: if (Q3) holds, shortest-path hop is NOT a fundamental acquisition-cost barrier for discovery-enabled acquisition and effort should move to discovery-channel coverage and substrate expansion; if it does not hold, record the engine-stratified bounded negative, close the discovery axis on this substrate class, and hand the persistence-maintenance axis (re-validation GETs/bytes plus stale-replay false-accept rate versus re-derivation cost, scaling with hop and elapsed time) to the next mandate.
allocation.rationale: Cognitive reset performed; this lane is deliberately moved off its local thread. Fresh look: with today's Codex and no handoff, Frontier would ask the single most architecture-changing, never-validly-measured question - whether the Web's own indexes (sitemaps, feeds, on-site search, JSON-LD) make deep acquisition O(1), which would retire traversal-and-cache as the optimization target and move effort to discovery coverage and substrate expansion. That question is genuinely Frontier's, but both prior attempts died on an unattainable prerequisite rather than on science: v1 (EXP-FRONTIER-37984242167) committed an EMPTY sampling frame (0 seeds, 0 DEEP items, 0 hosts) and no pre-freeze certificate; v2 (EXP-FRONTIER-38085197666) declared all six freeze_eligibility checks PASS while its own declared freeze_artifacts (design_probe/pool_confirmation.json, research/frontier/discovery_channels.py) are ABSENT from origin/lab2/frontier - verified at source - and failure.json records exit 65. The hard requirement of >= 3 DEEP items on >= 2 distinct engines is the failure point, and the parent found DEEP items on only a single engine (100% doc.rust-lang.org mdBook; EXP-FRONTIER-37950626378, VN-V8/VF-02, where the GROWING ratio was itself bounded as a level-order estimator artifact). Rather than spend a third cycle rediscovering the same absence, the mandate changes the measured object: attainability is measured, not assumed, so the design is always satisfiable and both outcomes - architectural shortcut exists, or discovery is not a shortcut on this substrate - are decision-changing. Runner-up considered and deliberately not chosen now: the persistence-maintenance/invalidation economics, which is attainable and feeds C-FRESHNESS/C-PRODUCT-ECON but is less basin-changing and is owned by Graph/Product; it is recorded as the conditional next step if Q3 returns a negative.

director_mandate.portfolio_assessment: 436 canonical experiments; effective claim state C-MEAS-VALID VALIDATED at the bounded authorship-separated real-Chromium scope (EXP-RUNTIME-36293257855); C-PARAM-INHERIT, C-FRESHNESS, C-DELTA-REPAIR, C-RESIDUAL-NOVELTY EXPERIMENTAL; C-LLM-INHERIT, C-PRODUCT-ECON, C-CROSSSITE, C-SEMANTIC-RESOLVE, C-WEB-DYNAMICS HYPOTHESIS. No frozen transaction is pending anywhere: all six lanes' active experiments are PREFREEZE and none has a freeze.json, so nothing must be completed under an old design. This cycle opened with a control-plane event, verified at source on origin/lab2/<lane>: graph, intel, physics and runtime all failed the DESIGN stage at 15:31-15:51 UTC with the SAME fingerprint (3b9ff5e4e9e73f23e368efb4, 'stage exited with code 1') while the Scout model was unavailable (rc=139) - one shared infrastructure outage, not four scientific design defects. Inspection of the actual specs separates cleanly: physics, intel and runtime had substantively complete designs (all six freeze_eligibility checks PASS with evidence refs; physics even pre-provisioned and pinned a distinct Tor egress at DESIGN) and lost only the review step; graph and product still carry the EMPTY spec template (claim_ids=[], question='', all six checks PENDING), so their designs never started. Frontier is different: its spec declares all six checks PASS but its own declared freeze_artifacts (design_probe/pool_confirmation.json, research/frontier/discovery_channels.py) are ABSENT from the branch and failure.json records exit 65 - a genuine design-contract failure whose root is an unattainable pre-freeze attainability prerequisite, not the outage. The strategic critical path is unchanged and confirmed by PROGRAM_AUDIT_GLOBAL_2026-10-10: the factory produces evidence but no validated external-agent product. The three gated blockers stand - B1 no shipped parameterized carrier (src/spider/kernel.py has no distill_parameterized and a 0.5/0.8 confidence mismatch), B2 benchmark degeneracy (cold/retrieval at the 1.0 correctness ceiling on the mandatory-discovery deterministic REST class), B3 unresolved same-model agent capability (0/5 and 0/5 on local 3B/7B). The three-conditions rule therefore forbids funding any full C-LLM-INHERIT / C-RESIDUAL-NOVELTY / C-PRODUCT-ECON four-arm execution this cycle; every lane is directed at a cheap prerequisite, a decidable local question, or an attainable measurement instead. Decision: CONTINUE Product on B1 (empty design, re-issued), Runtime on B2 (complete design, resume), Intel on B3 (complete design, resume), Physics on C-WEB-DYNAMICS vantage transfer (complete design, resume), Graph on C-SEMANTIC-RESOLVE joint-authorship confound removal (empty design, re-issued); PIVOT Frontier off the twice-blocked conditional-reachability design onto an attainability-first, always-satisfiable discovery census of the SAME architectural question. No lane is PARKed or TERMINATED: each has a high-value decidable next step and none is idle after this allocation. Local-attractor flags on graph, physics and runtime were treated as diagnostics; the cognitive reset confirmed the inherited direction on merits in each case.
